- Upper-right arm: (7,38), (8,37), ..., (17,28) - 11 dots
- Lower-left arm: (19,26), ..., (29,16) - 11 dots (but some already collected)
- Lower-right arm: (19,28), ..., (29,38) - 11 dots (but some already collected)
The diamond perimeter |row-cr| + |col-cc| = 9 is a rotated square. To cover an X arm, the diamond needs to be positioned so the arm lies on the diamond perimeter.

Actually, let me think about this more practically. The X arms are diagonal lines. The diamond perimeter has 4 sides, each a diagonal line segment. So each diamond position can cover parts of up to 4 X arms.
The best position [27, 27] covers 17 dots. Let me see what other high-yield positions exist and plan a path that visits them.
Actually, let me try a different approach. Instead of trying to calculate the optimal path manually, let me just execute the 4 LEFT moves and see what happens, then plan the next moves from there. The key insight is that I need to visit positions where the diamond perimeter covers many orange dots.

For now, let me just execute the 4 LEFT moves and see the result. Then I'll plan the next phase.

    counts[c] = counts.get(c, 0) + 1

c_children = set()
for n in c_nodes:
    c_children.update(n['children'])
free_o = [n for n in o_nodes if n['id'] not in c_children]
print(f"Free orange dots: {len(free_o)}")

# Get positions
o_positions = sorted([(n['boundary'][0][0], n['boundary'][0][1]) for n in free_o])
print(f"Positions: {o_positions}")
</parameter>
